description: Source of truth for local build and dev/start commands by runtime id. Populate runtimes with real project services/apps/workers and keep local environment script entrypoints current.

sharedInfra.policy: One shared devstack stack (~/.devstack) provides Postgres/Redis for every project on this machine; this repo holds its own tenant, never a repo-local Postgres/Redis container. See .claude/skills/devops/references/shared-local-infrastructure.md.
sharedInfra.reservedPortsNote: docs, mobile-metro, and ws were auto-claimed by `devstack adopt` from directory-presence heuristics (docs/, mobile/pubspec.yaml, @nestjs/websockets). None is an actual separate listening port today: docs/ is static markdown with no dev server, mobile/ is a Flutter app (no Metro bundler), and ChatGateway/AlarmsGateway attach socket.io to the same NestJS HTTP server as the api role. Only the api port is wired into scripts/. The reservations are kept (harmless, inside this project's own port block) so a future docs site, RN tooling, or standalone ws gateway does not need a new claim.

legacyCompose.note: postgres/redis services parked behind the `legacy` Compose profile by `devstack adopt --apply` (backup: backend/docker-compose.yml.devstack-backup.1787195883); `docker compose up` no longer starts them. The `backend`/`nginx` services in the same file remain for the unrelated VPS/production image build (api-cupid.tikup.me), not local dev.
legacyCompose.dataMigration: postgres data dumped from the local cupid-apps-postgres-1 container and restored into the shared tenant (backup at ~/.devstack/backups/cupid-apps/cupid.20260820T031803Z.sql); restored objects were reassigned from the shared admin role to the cupid_apps tenant role after restore (pg_dump/restore left them admin-owned, which blocked the tenant role from reading its own data). redis data was NOT migrated (devstack adopt does not support automatic Redis migration); the legacy cupid-apps-redis-1 container was stopped, not removed, in case old cache/session data still needs manual copying.

localPortPolicy.devstackProjectName: Derived by scripts/lib/common.sh devstack_project_name() from the repo directory name (e.g. cupid-apps); used to pass --project to devstack CLI calls that don't take a path. The devstack CLI derives the same project name itself when given the repo path.
localPortPolicy.dependencyPublishDefault: Local dependency services (Postgres, Redis) are never repo-local; this project consumes its private tenant on the shared devstack stack (~/.devstack), reached over the loopback host ports devstack assigns (see sharedInfra above). No fixed 5432/6379 host bindings, no repo-local dependency containers.
localPortPolicy.hostBindingRule: Application ports come only from `devstack port claim`/`devstack port pin` (see sharedInfra.reservedPorts); never scan for a free port or hardcode a framework default.

portRecordFields.name: logical port name such as postgres, api, web, redis

setup.purpose: Set up local infrastructure such as Docker or Compose containers, volumes, dependency services, and readiness checks.
setup.verification: bash -n scripts/setup.sh, shellcheck when available, executable bit, execution or typed blocker

build.purpose: Install project dependencies and build all frontend, backend, worker, job, generated, and shared components.
build.verification: bash -n scripts/build.sh, shellcheck when available, executable bit, execution or typed blocker

startDev.purpose: Verify or start local infrastructure and run all modules needed for local development in dev/watch mode when supported.
startDev.verification: bash -n scripts/start-dev.sh, shellcheck when available, executable bit, bounded startup smoke with readiness and shutdown or typed blocker

startProd.purpose: Run the project in production mode from built artifacts or production commands with config preflight and readiness checks.
startProd.verification: bash -n scripts/start-prod.sh, shellcheck when available, executable bit, production-mode startup smoke when safe or typed blocker

port.hostPortSource: devstack port claim --role api (see sharedInfra.reservedPorts.api); never a scanned or hardcoded port

backend-api.notes: scripts/start-dev.sh and scripts/start-prod.sh run the backend directly on the host via npm (not the backend service in backend/docker-compose.yml), so nest watch mode works and the Firebase secret is never baked into a Docker image for local use. scripts/setup.sh no longer starts any repo-local Postgres/Redis container: it runs `devstack use` to adopt/refresh this project's tenant on the shared devstack stack (~/.devstack) and `devstack port check`, then start-dev.sh/start-prod.sh source the generated .env.devstack contract for POSTGRES_HOST/PORT/USER/PASSWORD/DB and the reserved api port (see sharedInfra above). Backend cannot boot without backend/service-account.json (Firebase Admin credential), which is a manually supplied local secret never generated by an agent.

engines.note: astro@6.0.5 requires Node >=22.12.0; this machine's default node is v20.20.2, so scripts/build.sh, scripts/start-dev.sh and CI must not rely on an unpinned ambient node.

port.hostPortSource: devstack port claim --role web (see sharedInfra.reservedPorts.web); never a scanned or hardcoded port

web-frontend.dependsOnRationale: web-frontend is a pure static Astro marketing site (astro.config output: 'static'); web/package.json declares only the `astro` dependency, no HTTP client (no axios, no fetch-based API client module), and every page under web/src/pages sources its content from local static data modules in web/src/data/*.ts, not from backend-api or any other runtime service. There is no repo-local Postgres/Redis usage, no worker dependency, and no runtime call to backend-api at build or request time (OQ-REQ006-2 RESOLVED). It is deployed as a prebuilt static directory to the VPS host Caddy for cupidus.app, so `dependsOn: []` is correct rather than an omission.
web-frontend.notes: Static Astro build (output: 'static'), no API dependency (OQ-REQ006-2 RESOLVED), no backend/worker/postgres/redis dependency. scripts/build.sh runs `npm ci` + `npm run check` (astro check, type-checks; astro build alone does not) + `npm run build`. scripts/start-dev.sh runs `npm run dev -- --port "$DEVSTACK_PORT_WEB" --host 127.0.0.1`, sourcing the port from .env.devstack (never Astro's default 4321). Deployed as a static directory to the VPS host Caddy for cupidus.app (see .github/workflows/deploy-web.yml); no container image, no GHCR.

sdk.note: Flutter SDK lives at /Users/alantravala/flutter on this machine and is not on the shell PATH; root scripts and this registry entry resolve it via FLUTTER_SDK_PATH (default $HOME/flutter) rather than assuming a bare `flutter` command resolves.

launch.purpose: Interactive developer launch path: boot an Android emulator or iOS Simulator when none is running, wait for Flutter to report the device, then hand off to a foreground `flutter run -d <device>` session.

subcommands.android: Reuses the first adb device already in 'device' state. Otherwise boots an AVD (`--avd <name>`, else the first entry from `emulator -list-avds`) and polls `getprop sys.boot_completed` until it returns 1. Device id passed to `flutter run -d` is the adb serial, e.g. emulator-5554.
subcommands.ios: macOS only; exits non-zero with IOS_UNSUPPORTED_HOST elsewhere. Reuses an already-Booted simulator, otherwise picks the first available iPhone (or first available device) from `xcrun simctl list devices available` and boots it with `xcrun simctl boot`. Device id passed to `flutter run -d` is the simulator UDID.

options.--avd <name>: Android only. Boot this AVD instead of the first listed one.
options.--udid <id>: Skip device selection and use this exact adb serial (android) or simulator UDID (ios).
options.-- <args>: Everything after `--` is forwarded to `flutter run`, e.g. --dart-define=CUPID_API_BASE_URL=http://10.0.2.2:3000.

androidSdk.note: On this machine the SDK is at /Users/alantravala/Library/Android/sdk with neither ANDROID_HOME nor ANDROID_SDK_ROOT exported. platform-tools/adb happens to be on PATH but emulator/ and cmdline-tools/ are not, so android_tool() searches the SDK subdirectories rather than assuming bare `emulator` resolves.

timeouts.note: Both waits are bounded via scripts/lib/common.sh wait_for(), so a device that never comes up fails with a typed blocker instead of hanging.

launch.verification: bash -n scripts/run-mobile.sh, shellcheck when available, executable bit, bounded device boot plus `flutter devices` visibility check or typed blocker

readiness.description: Live probe per devops/SKILL.md 14b1: a Flutter app exposes no socket to poll, so readiness launches the installed app on an already-booted device and asserts the OS reports its launcher activity as the resumed (foreground) activity. Only a running app process can satisfy this; it fails while nothing is running.
readiness.command: adb -s "$MOBILE_DEVICE_SERIAL" shell am start -W -n com.snapsofts.cupid/com.snapsofts.cupid_mobile.MainActivity >/dev/null && for _ in $(seq 1 30); do adb -s "$MOBILE_DEVICE_SERIAL" shell dumpsys activity activities | grep -q "ResumedActivity.*com.snapsofts.cupid/com.snapsofts.cupid_mobile.MainActivity" && exit 0; sleep 2; done; exit 1
preconditions: A device/emulator is booted and visible to adb; MOBILE_DEVICE_SERIAL is its adb serial (e.g. emulator-5554). scripts/run-mobile.sh android boots one when none is running.
The debug APK from buildCommand is installed on that device (flutter install -d $MOBILE_DEVICE_SERIAL, or a prior flutter run).
readiness.iosCommand: xcrun simctl launch "$MOBILE_DEVICE_UDID" com.snapsofts.cupid && for _ in $(seq 1 30); do xcrun simctl spawn "$MOBILE_DEVICE_UDID" launchctl list | grep -q com.snapsofts.cupid && exit 0; sleep 2; done; exit 1

inAppFirstScreenSignal.note: In-app marker for the first screen, asserted by `flutter test` (mobile/test/features/home/home_screen_test.dart). Retained as supporting evidence only: a widget test is build/test-shaped and passes while no app process exists, so it is NOT the readiness probe (devops/SKILL.md 14b1).

mobile-app.dependsOnRationale: The app issues live REST calls to backend-api through the generated CupidApi/Dio client (mobile/lib/core/network/cupid_api_client.dart), whose base URL is the compile-time CUPID_API_BASE_URL (mobile/lib/core/config/cupid_api_config.dart, default http://localhost:3000; note that default is stale now that backend-api's shared-devstack port is 21020, not 3000 -- see sharedInfra.reservedPorts.api above). Since STORY-059's shared-infra adoption, launching against the local backend requires --dart-define=CUPID_API_BASE_URL=http://10.0.2.2:21020 from an Android emulator (10.0.2.2 is the emulator alias for the host loopback) or http://127.0.0.1:21020 from an iOS simulator; updating the compile-time default itself is mobile-dev scope, not covered by this DevOps change. Auth, pairing, chat, timeline, expenses, gallery, pet, reminders, dream-jar, and love-contract features all read through that client, so backend-api must be reachable before the app is functionally usable.
mobile-app.notes: scripts/start-dev.sh runs `flutter pub get` + `flutter test` as the dev readiness signal, and scripts/build.sh runs a real `flutter build apk --debug` as the build verification step. Actually launching the app now has a dedicated entrypoint, `scripts/run-mobile.sh <android|ios>` (see the `launch` block above), which boots an emulator/simulator when needed and hands off to `flutter run -d <device>`. That path is deliberately interactive and foreground-owned by `flutter run`: it is a human developer path, not a headless or CI path, so start-dev.sh's readiness gate still does not invoke it.
